## Metrics

The federation-health instrument set served by `GET /metrics`. Names and label keys are
constants in `metrics::names` — **this table mirrors that module; change them together.**
Counters are constructed *without* the `_total` suffix (the Prometheus exporter appends it;
a unit test in `metrics.rs` pins the rendered names). All instruments record through the
typed `AppState.metrics` handle; when `[telemetry] metrics_enabled = false` the same handle
drops measurements at the SDK boundary, so call sites never branch.

| Rendered name | Type | Labels | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | `route` (matched template or `unmatched`), `status_class` | `metrics::http_metrics_middleware` (outside the rate limiter → 429s count; inside CORS → preflights don't) |
| `firehose_subscribers` | gauge | — | `SubscriberGuard` in `sync_subscribe_repos.rs` (+1 connect, −1 on any exit path) |
| `firehose_events_total` | counter | `frame` (`commit`/`account`/`identity`/`sync`) | `Firehose::broadcast` — the single fan-out choke point |
| `firehose_backfill_window_seconds` | gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each sweep (age of `MIN(sequenced_at)`; 0 when the log is empty) |
| `firehose_gc_swept_total` / `firehose_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each completed pass |
| `labeler_watch_changes_total` / `labeler_watch_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `labeler_watch.rs` after each completed pass (`changes` = label rows upserted + removed; error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_gc_swept_total` / `blob_gc_errors_total` / `blob_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / counter / gauge | — | `blob_gc.rs` after each completed pass (a failed-to-start pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm). `errors` counts **failures**, of two kinds sharing one counter because both mean "the pass left work undone": one per account whose reconcile errored, and one per expired ownership row the sweep failed to delete. A failed account is excluded from the sweep entirely (fail closed — its references could not be computed, so its blobs must not be collected) and leaks disk until the fault is fixed. Note it contributes exactly **1** regardless of how many blobs go uncollected — the account that motivated this counter reports `1` while leaving 534 blobs behind; the per-account blob count is the `blobs_skipped` log field, not this metric. A skipped account is a distinct fault from "the sweep is dead", so it gets a distinct channel: a nonzero `errors` beside a *fresh* timestamp is its alarm. `sweep_status`'s `SweepRun::errors` mirrors it for `GET /v1/admin/health` |
| `blob_mirror_synced_total` / `blob_mirror_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `blob_mirror/mod.rs` after each completed pass (`synced` = bucket uploads + deletes; a failed-to-enumerate pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_scrub_flagged_total` / `blob_scrub_healed_total` / `blob_scrub_last_run_timestamp` | counter / counter / gauge | — | `blob_scrub.rs` after each completed pass (`flagged` = unhealed integrity problems this pass — missing files, hash/size mismatches, orphan files; `healed` = bad/missing files repaired from the blob-mirror bucket; a failed-to-list pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose). `routes/get_blob.rs` also adds to `flagged` when a serve-time re-hash catches a corrupt file — same alarm channel, so an operator watches one counter |
| `account_reaper_swept_total` / `account_reaper_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `account_reaper.rs` after each completed pass |
| `agent_claim_sweep_swept_total` / `agent_claim_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `agent_claim_sweep.rs` after each completed pass (error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `admin_nonce_sweep_swept_total` / `admin_nonce_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `admin_nonce_sweep.rs` after each completed pass |
| `relay_crawl_requests_total` | counter | `outcome` (`ok`/`rejected`/`exhausted`) | `crawler.rs` per finished notification |
| `proxy_requests_total` | counter | `upstream` (`appview`/`chat`/`moderation`/`header_target` — the last for an `app.bsky.*`/`chat.bsky.*` request that used an `atproto-proxy` header to override its default), `status_class` | `app.rs::xrpc_handler` on both the streaming and munged paths |
| `proxy_upstream_lag_seconds` | histogram | — | `read_after_write/mod.rs`, same conditional value as the `Atproto-Upstream-Lag` header |
| `rate_limit_rejections_total` | counter | `limiter` (`global_ip`/`endpoint_ip`/`account_writes`) | `rate_limit.rs` middleware; `record_write.rs` for write points |
| `migration_imports_total` | counter | `outcome` (`ok`/`error`) | `routes/import_repo.rs` |
| `notify_queue_depth` | gauge | — | `notify_relay_client.rs` on both edges of the send queue: `NotifySender::send` increments, and the worker decrements **after** the job finishes, so the depth counts outstanding work rather than only what is waiting (during the relay outage this metric exists for, each job burns the full 30s stream timeout, and a single stuck job is real backlog). The queue is unbounded by design — a trigger must never block on a push relay — so this is the one quantity a prolonged outage grows without limit, previously inferable only from `warn!` volume. Not recorded at all when no relay is configured (no worker exists). `GET /v1/admin/health`'s `notifyQueueDepth` mirrors it for operators, reading the same counter directly so it works with `[telemetry] metrics_enabled` off (the `sweep_status.rs` arrangement), and reports `null` rather than `0` when the feature is unconfigured |

Cardinality rule: label values are always drawn from small fixed sets or the route table —
never from request data (raw URIs, rkeys, DIDs, hostnames).

## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. If it's an XRPC procedure: a JSON input body is parsed with `LexiconInput<T>` (never bare
   `axum::Json<T>`) after vendoring its lexicon document (`crates/pds/lexicons/README.md`); a
   no-input procedure takes `NoInputBody` instead. Both must be the handler's final extractor.
5. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
6. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root AGENTS.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

1. Identify the owning entity (`accounts`, `oauth`, etc.).
2. Add the function to the matching `db/<entity>.rs` file.
3. If no matching file exists, create one with `// pattern: Imperative Shell`.
4. Export the function and any new data struct via `db/mod.rs` (`pub mod <entity>;`).

  let {
    onfresh,
    onexisting,
    onlostwallet,
    onservergone,

    /** Make a brand-new identity — the create ceremony (method choice one level in). */

    onlostwallet: () => void;

    onservergone: () => void;
    /** Absent on first launch, where there is no home to go back to. */

  } = $props();
</script>

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-27

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `foreign-pds` (a spec-compliant non-Custos host — advertises no
  capabilities, so the create flow's gate closes and steers to import),
  `unreachable-pds` (the same empty capability list, but `reached: false` — the gate must
  show a retryable error, never the steer), `one-identity`, `multi-identity`,
  `alert-active`, plus its three siblings covering the rest of the recovery-window
  urgency ladder — `alert-warning` (~12h left), `alert-critical` (~3h left) and
  `alert-expired` (past the window, the only way to reach `AlertDetailScreen`'s
  disabled "Recovery window expired" button); the four differ only in how old the
  seeded change is, since that is what `getUrgency` reads. `alert-multi` seeds TWO alarmed
  identities at different ages — the only preset that reaches the multi-identity half of the
  launch takeover (which lands on Protection rather than on one identity's alarm surface)
  and Protection's "Not now" exit. `notifications-unverified` (the Settings notification diagnostic with something to report — the breadcrumbs are written by the Notification Service Extension, which exists only on a device and only runs when a real sealed push arrives, and `window.__harness.state()` is a deep CLONE rather than the live store, so a scenario is the only way in; it seeds two key-desync failures beside one benign post-restart one, so the readout has to level correctly rather than describe whichever it saw first), `device-key-unusable` (a device restored from an encrypted backup: the
  device-key metadata came back, the Secure Enclave key did not — the only way to reach the
  "can no longer sign" degraded state in a browser with no enclave), `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue); plus the escrow-less kit pair: `self-held-kit` (a claimed identity on a
  non-Custos host — device key at `rotationKeys[0]`, a longer claimed tail than the
  re-key's `[device, PDS]`, no recovery key, host advertises nothing) and
  `self-held-kit-escrow-host` (the same identity after the kit, now hosted somewhere that
  DOES advertise `escrow` — the upsell seam's only true state). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getPdsCapabilities()`/`hasPdsCapability()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and the did:web wrappers (`prepareDidWebCeremony()`/`completeDidWebCeremony()` — the create-flow did:web ceremony, returning `DidWebPreparation`/`DIDCeremonyResult`; `importDidWebIdentity()` — bring an existing did:web under wallet management, returning `ImportedDidWebIdentity`, error `ImportDidWebError`; `buildDidWebMigrationDocument()`/`submitDidWebMigrationDocument()` — compose + publish-verify the did:web outbound-migration identity leg, type `DidWebMigrationDocument`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `createDestinationAccount()`, `transferRepo()`, `transferBlobs(did, acceptLoss)`, `transferPreferences()`, `verifyImport()`, `armIdentityLeg()`, `finalizeMigration()`) with types (`AccountStatus`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`, `BlobLoss`, `BlobTransferDirection`), the sovereign change-handle wrappers (`getIdentityHandleDomains()`, `changeHandle()` — biometric-gated) with type `HandleChangeError`, and the unlock wrappers (`getIdentityUnlockRoute()`, `unlockIdentityWithPassword()`) with types (`UnlockRoute`, `UnlockMethod`, `UnlockError`), and and identity-removal wrappers (`getIdentityRemovalRoute()`, `requestIdentityRemoval()`, `confirmIdentityRemoval()`, `tombstoneIdentity()`, `listPendingRemovals()`, `forgetIdentityLocally()`) with types (`RemovalError`, `RemovalOutcome`, `RemovalRoute`), and the share-recovery wrappers (`startShareRecovery()`, `addRecoveryShare()`, `removeRecoveryShare()`, `initiateEscrowRelease()`, `requestEscrowRelease()`, `verifyRecoveryShares()`, `recoverIdentity()` — biometric-gated, `runRecoveryEpilogue()`, `getPendingRecoveryEpilogue()`, `confirmRecoveryBackup()`) with types (`ShareRecoveryError`, `CollectedShare`, `RecoveryTarget`, `EscrowReleaseStatus`, `RecoveredIdentity`, `RecoveryAnchor`, `EpilogueResult`, `PendingEpilogue`), and the media-backup wrappers (`getBlobBackupStatus()`, `setBlobBackupEnabled()`, `runBlobBackup()`, `restoreBlobBackup()` — biometric-gated, and the app-global background-sweep settings `getBackgroundBackupSettings()` / `setBackgroundBackupSettings()`) with types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`, `BackupLocation`, `BlobBackupError`, `BackgroundBackupSettings`, `BackgroundBackupError`), and the repo-backup wrappers (`getRepoBackupStatus()`, `setRepoBackupEnabled()`, `runRepoBackup()`, `exportRepoBackup()` — none biometric-gated; all read the public `getRepo` or local disk) with types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`, `RepoBackupError`), and the push-notification wrappers (`registerForNotifications()`, `refreshNotificationSenderKeys()`, `getNotificationDiagnostics()`, `clearNotificationFailures()` — none biometric-gated; nothing is signed and no identity material is exposed) with types (`RegistrationOutcome`, `RegistrationStatus`, `SenderKey`, `SenderKeyPinning`, `NotificationDiagnostics`, `NotificationFailure`, `NotificationFailureReason`, `NotificationsError`), and the notification-tap routing wrapper (`takePendingNotificationRoute()` + `NOTIFICATION_ROUTE_EVENT`) with type `PendingNotificationRoute`
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — one screen component per step of the create / import / recover onboarding flows (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory; hand-counted lists here drifted twice)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — the home-surface screen components (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory) plus the DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). **ProtectionScreen is the app-level Defend surface** (the `protection` step), opened from the home list's protection strip — which is a **door, not a readout**: the PLC monitor runs unattended and, before this surface existed, produced nothing a user could look at, so the wallet's central trust claim rested on an assertion. It opens with a `StatusPanel` over the whole wallet, then every identity's status row (ordered most-severe-first by `$lib/protection`; an alarmed row taps straight through to `alert_detail`, every other row to the identity panel), then the monitor history — the sweep log from `getMonitorHistory`, with a "Check now" action whose result lands in that log. The strip and the panel render the SAME `summarize()` output, so the door can never state something the room contradicts, and `identityReturnStep` (the tier-up sibling of `alertReturnStep`) keeps Back from ejecting someone working the list. It takes a `takeover` prop for the multi-identity alarm landing: the app put the user here, so the exit is rendered as a labelled **"Not now"** pill (`ScreenHeader`'s `backText`) rather than the icon-only chevron, whose `backLabel` is an accessible name only and would otherwise leave a sighted user with no visible way to decline. **IdentityScreen is the per-identity instrument panel** (the `identity_detail` step) and the spine of the home-surface IA: state leads, actions follow. It opens with a `StatusPanel` derived from `$lib/identity-status`, then a **Use** zone (sign in to an app / sign in to Bluesky / my agents), then two doors — **MoveOrRebuildScreen** (`move_or_rebuild`: outbound migration + sovereign disaster recovery, an exit kept findable rather than filed under maintenance) and **ManageIdentityScreen** (`manage_identity`: change handle, backups, DID document, plus an Advanced entry). **AdvancedToolsScreen** (`advanced_tools`) is the vestibule: a plain-language framing card stating what protocol-level tools do, then the surgery list (add a recovery key, rotate repo signing key, repair hosting endpoint, remove identity). The vestibule is **additive framing only** — every operation keeps its own biometric gate, pre-sign review, and hold-to-confirm. SecurityCheckup is the quiet disclosure hanging off a secure StatusPanel (key custody, public-record watch, media + posts backup freshness), all reads of state the wallet already holds. ChangeHandleScreen is the sovereign change-handle surface reached from ManageIdentityScreen's "Change handle" row (did:plc + device-key-as-root only): it loads the hosting PDS's served domains, pre-flights the session (`ensureIdentitySession`, `unlockIdentity` on `NEEDS_UNLOCK`), then runs the biometric-gated `changeHandle`. AppPasswordsScreen is the app-password surface reached from the identity screen's Use zone ("Sign in to Bluesky"): it lists/mints/revokes the account's scoped app passwords via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (SESSION_LOCKED → `unlockIdentity` + retry ($lib/unlock: sovereign login on a Custos host, password prompt elsewhere); mint and revoke are biometric-gated; the generated secret is shown once with copy and never persisted). MediaBackupScreen is the user-held blob-backup surface reached from ManageIdentityScreen's "Backups" row (media and posts are presented as one item because they are one job): opt-in with the mirror size always shown, "Back up now" (incremental, CID-verified sync pass over public sync endpoints — no session), and a biometric-gated "Restore to server" (`uploadBlob` via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`; SESSION_LOCKED → `unlockIdentity` + retry ($lib/unlock: sovereign login on a Custos host, password prompt elsewhere)), with per-blob failures listed rather than aborting the run. The same screen also holds a "Back up your posts" section (`repo_backup.rs`): opt-in with the snapshot size + last-backup shown, and "Back up posts now" (a full-CAR `getRepo` snapshot, validated client-side before it replaces the prior copy — no session, no biometric); there is no repo "restore" button (an `importRepo` needs a deactivated account, so restore flows through migration). `+page.svelte` fires silent opportunistic `runBlobBackup` **and** `runRepoBackup` passes on app open for opted-in identities (each on its own per-DID flag). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection. RemoveIdentityScreen is the permanent-removal flow (warn → emailed-code (+ password) → biometric-gated hold-to-remove → progress, with a "tombstone pending, retry" state), reached from AdvancedToolsScreen's destructive `onremove` (behind the vestibule). The password field is shown only when `getIdentityRemovalRoute` says the identity's host needs it: where the host advertises `walletAccountDelete` the wallet signs a device-key removal proof instead, so the confirm step is the code alone — an identity created without a password has nothing to type there, and the warning copy stays silent about a credential until the route resolves rather than promising one it may drop. Offered for **both** DID methods, with the screen branching on `did:web:` throughout: the warning drops the "retire on the network by tombstoning" promise (a did:web has no tombstone), the escape hatch's advanced "also retire on the network" option is withheld (it could not do what it says), and a successful removal ends in the `web_epilogue` state rather than returning to the identity list — the DID keeps resolving until its `did.json` leaves the domain, which only whoever controls that domain can do. The screen switches on the outcome's `tombstoneCid` being null (the backend's honest report that no tombstone was published), not on the DID string alone
- `src/lib/appearance.ts` — in-app appearance override (System / Light / Dark): `normalizePreference()` / `toColorScheme()` (pure, tested by `appearance.test.ts`), `readLocalMirror()`, `initAppearance()` (launch-time reconcile: re-asserts the localStorage mirror, then reads the Keychain via IPC and lets it win), `setAppearance()` (applies the inline `color-scheme` override on `<html>` instantly, writes the mirror, then persists to the Keychain). The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth
- `src/lib/agent-scopes.ts` — plain-language descriptions of granular OAuth scope tokens for the agent-consent surfaces: `describeScope(token)` / `describeScopes(tokens)` return `{ summary, token, elevated }` (the raw token is always shown alongside the human sentence; `account:*`/`identity:*`/full-access grants are flagged `elevated`; an unknown token falls back to showing itself, never a vague label). Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`
- `src/lib/deadline.ts` — PLC recovery deadline utilities: `getDeadline(createdAt)` (adds 72h to ISO 8601 timestamp), `getUrgency(deadline)` (returns `'safe'` | `'warning'` | `'critical'` | `'expired'`), `formatCountdown(deadline)` (human-readable `"Xh Ym remaining"`). `Urgency` type exported. Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: three-flow state machine starting at `add_identity` (`AddIdentityScreen` — **one situation question**, "Add an identity — what's your situation?", replacing the old create/import/recover door taxonomy: `onfresh` opens `identity_method`, `IdentityMethodScreen` — the did:plc / did:web method fork; `onexisting` opens `identity_input`; `onlostwallet` opens `recover_start`; `onservergone` opens `server_gone`). **Create flow:** add_identity -> `identity_method` -> [did:plc: pds_config; new did:web: `did_web_path` -> `did_web_domain` -> pds_config] -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony (the did:web branch runs `did_web_ceremony` instead) -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). `complete` goes **straight to `home`**: there is no post-create OAuth round trip and no browser hand-off (see the Key Decision below). `pds_config` is a **capability gate**, not just a form: after `savePdsUrl` (which re-probes the host, so this reads a warm cache) it calls `getPdsCapabilities()` and, unless the host advertises `createCeremony`, routes to `create_unavailable` (`CreateUnavailableScreen`) instead of `claim_code` — the create ceremony is Custos-structural, so a standard PDS is refused before the user types an account detail rather than failing inside `/v1/accounts/mobile`. This is the one gate that reads `ServerCapabilities.reached`: it does not merely withhold a feature, it tells the user their server cannot create identities, and a host that could not be asked must produce a retryable error instead of that accusation. The gate covers both create paths, since the did:web branch also passes through `pds_config`. From `create_unavailable` the import flow is one tap away with the chosen server still configured. **Import flow:** add_identity -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Existing did:web** takes the third `identity_method` branch: `did_web_path` (choose "existing") -> `did_web_existing`, which calls `importDidWebIdentity()` to bring the live document under wallet management, then enters the method-agnostic outbound-migration flow at `migration_start` (a did:web has no claim ceremony — control is proven by the domain publish and the source-PDS password, not a PLC op). **Home:** home -> { protection (the app-level Defend surface, from the protection strip) | identity_detail (the instrument panel) -> { move_or_rebuild -> { migration_start | recovery_rebuild_start } | manage_identity -> { change_handle | media_backup | did_document | advanced_tools -> { self_held_kit_review | rotate_repo_key | endpoint_repair | remove_identity } } | app_passwords | my_agents | oauth_consent_approval | alert_detail -> recovery_override } }, with `protection` itself reaching `identity_detail` and `alert_detail`. Each re-homed screen's `onback` returns to the door it now hangs off, which is the only spatial model this flat step union has. Two surfaces are reachable from more than one place, so each records where it came from rather than assuming: `alert_detail` (home's card strip, the identity panel's critical status, or a Protection row) via `alertReturnStep`, and `identity_detail` (the home list or a Protection row) via `identityReturnStep`. A fixed back path would eject the user out of the identity they were standing in, or out of the list they were working through. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` **or** `protection` step — Protection's whole subject is how fresh the reading is, so it is the worst place to sit showing a stale one. **Alarm takeover landing:** that check — on launch and on every foreground — hands its answer to `$lib/alarm-landing`'s `decideAlarmLanding`, and the page lands on the alarm rather than leaving it behind the protection strip: one alarmed identity opens `alert_detail`, more than one opens `protection` (already ordered most-urgent-first by `$lib/protection`). Landing precedence is the `onMount` ordering itself — a stranded removal and a pending recovery epilogue are resolved first and the takeover runs only in the branch where neither did, because interrupted key-material handling outranks re-showing an alarm the user has already been told about; `landOnAlarm` re-checks that the app is still on `home`/`protection` before it moves, since the directory round trip can land after the user has navigated. Every takeover is dismissible: both landings' exits read **"Not now"** (`AlertDetailScreen`'s `backLabel`, `ProtectionScreen`'s `takeover`, both driven by the `alarmTakeover` flag `goTo` clears) and returns to a home the strip and card treatments already render in alarm state. Alarms the takeover has presented are recorded in the in-session `shownAlarms` set keyed by `alarmKey` (DID + sorted change CIDs), so a dismissed alarm does not re-take the app on the next foreground but a *new* unauthorized operation against the same identity does. The set is deliberately not persisted — an attack must not be dismissible once, forever

**Guarantees:**
- SSR is disabled globally (`ssr = false` in `src/routes/+layout.ts`); the frontend is a fully static SPA loaded from disk by WKWebView
- Build output lands in `dist/` (configured via `pages: 'dist'` in `svelte.config.js`)
- Frontend calls Tauri commands only through the `src/lib/ipc/` modules (imported from `$lib/ipc`) — no raw `invoke()` calls in page components
- PDS error codes from `create_account` are mapped back to the originating screen (e.g. EXPIRED_CODE -> claim_code step, EMAIL_TAKEN -> email step)

**Expects:**
- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command running the **client-share ceremony** (ceremony inversion): fetches the PDS signing key (GET /v1/repo-signing-key), loads-or-generates the client-side share set via `share_ceremony::load_or_create` (recovery seed + `derive_recovery_keypair` + 2-of-3 v2 envelope split, staged in the `ceremony-staging` Keychain slot BEFORE any network call so a retry reuses the identical set/set_id), builds the signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_multi_rotation_with_external_signer` with `rotationKeys = [device, recovery, PDS]` (ADR-0027) using the device key as signer, POSTs the op + password + `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (the Share 2 envelope — the only share Custos ever sees) to POST /v1/dids, persists DID + upgraded session token in Keychain, writes the wallet-generated Share 1 envelope to the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with a read-back verify (same convention as the re-key flow, so a second identity's ceremony cannot overwrite the first's Share 1), and returns `{ did, share3, share3Words }` to the frontend
- `src/lib.rs::confirm_share_backup(did: String) -> Result<(), ShareBackupError>` — Tauri IPC command: the ceremony teardown gate. Verifies the ceremony DID's Share 1 is durably present in `recovery-share-1:{did}` (else `SHARE_NOT_STORED` — the staging slot must not be destroyed while it is the seed's only home), then deletes the `ceremony-staging` slot (the seed's and Share 2's last local copy). The `did` is threaded from the ceremony result so the check reads the exact identity just created (mirrors the re-key epilogue's `confirm_rekey`). Idempotent; invoked by the frontend when the Shamir backup screen's confirmation completes
- `src/share_ceremony.rs` — client-side share generation module: `CeremonyShareSet` (recovery key did:key + the three base32 envelope strings + the Share 3 word phrase, all share material in `Zeroizing`), `load_or_create(handle, pds_url)` (reuse a valid staged set or generate + stage a fresh one; the staging record stores the three envelopes only — the seed is recomputed via `combine_envelopes(share1, share2)` on load), `clear_staging()` (idempotent teardown), `STAGING_ACCOUNT` (`"ceremony-staging"`). **Fail-closed staging contract:** only a genuinely absent slot, or one staged for different ceremony inputs (a new handle/PDS is the user's explicit abandonment of the old attempt), permits fresh generation; a present-but-unreadable/corrupt record errors with `StagingCorrupt` and preserves the slot — it may be the exact set a prior attempt already bound to a genesis op and escrowed, so overwriting it would permanently destroy the recovery seed
- `src/share_recovery.rs` — the "Recover existing identity" ceremony (10 Tauri IPC commands), the consuming inverse of `share_ceremony.rs`: `start_share_recovery(identifier)` (resolve handle/did:plc via plc.directory, then auto-load Share 1 via `auto_load_share1`: the resolved DID's iCloud-synchronizable per-DID slot, then its device-local per-DID slot, then the legacy global `recovery-share-1`, taking the first tier holding a valid v2 index-1 envelope), `add_recovery_share(share)` (base32 or word-phrase entry; A revoked refresh (400/401) and a host change both delete the dead record; a rate limit keeps it. Coalescing is a re-read (not a shared future): the second caller for one DID waits on the lock, then re-loads the freshly-persisted record — so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection. Thin XRPC wrappers + response types (`AppPasswordCreated`, `AppPasswordEntry`) live in `pds_client.rs`; a 409 duplicate name maps to `DUPLICATE_NAME`. `AppPasswordsError` (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, DUPLICATE_NAME, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/blob_backup.rs` — User-held blob backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up media" surface): `get_blob_backup_status(did)` (mirror location + opt-in flag + mirror size), `set_blob_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_blob_backup(did)` (incremental sync pass: paginated public `com.atproto.sync.listBlobs` → diff against the manifest → `getBlob` with Content-Type capture → **recompute the CIDv1 raw-codec SHA-256 CID and compare before writing** → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/blobs/{cid}` → append to the per-DID manifest `{root}/manifests/{sanitized-did}.json` (`cid, mimeType, size, fetchedAt`), saved after every blob so an interrupted run resumes; per-blob failures land in the report, never abort the run), and `restore_blob_backup(did)` (walk the manifest, re-verify each file's hash, `uploadBlob` with the stored MIME type over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED`, the `unlockIdentity` retry cue; an undownloaded iCloud placeholder or corrupt file is a per-blob failure with guidance). The mirror root resolves: `EZPDS_BLOB_BACKUP_DIR` env override (tests/dev) → the iCloud Drive ubiquity container `Documents/` on iOS (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier` via `objc2-foundation`, iOS-only target dep; user-visible in the Files app) → on a real device with iCloud off, `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` (never a silent local fallback) → elsewhere (macOS/simulator) a local app-data dir reported as `location: "local"`. A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `src/self_held_kit.rs` — the **escrow-less self-held Shamir kit** (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Add a recovery key" on the identity screen): the `rekey.rs` ceremony minus the escrow, for a claimed identity whose device key holds `rotationKeys[0]` but whose host is not Custos. `build_self_held_kit(did)` (generate + stage a client-side seed / 2-of-3 v2 envelope split in the per-DID `self-held-kit-staging:{did}` slot BEFORE any network call, prove eligibility, return the additive diff + the host's URL), `submit_self_held_kit(did)` (device-key-sign a PLC rotation op inserting the derived recovery key directly after the device key — the whole current tail shifts down one index, nothing is removed — POST it to plc.directory, write Share 1 to the per-DID iCloud-synchronizable slot with read-back verify, refresh the cached log + doc, record the `{did}:self-held-kit` marker; biometric-gated in the frontend), `confirm_self_held_kit(did)` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_rekey`: Share 1 must be verifiably durable before the staging slot — the last local home of Shares 2 and 3 — is destroyed), `self_held_kit_in_progress_cmd(did)`, and `self_held_kit_escrow_offer_cmd(did)` (the upsell **seam**: true only when the marker is present AND the identity's *current* host advertises `escrow`, so it is never true right after a kit completes). **Share 1 → Keychain; Shares 2 AND 3 → the user** — with no escrow there is no third party, and the sovereign recovery path already reconstructs from any two. **plc.directory is the only peer for anything touching the identity** (audit-log read, op submit, cache refresh); the sole request reaching the hosting PDS is the public, unauthenticated `describeServer` capability probe that proves the host offers no escrow — often served from the `pds_capabilities` cache, carrying no share material and no credential. No session, no `/v1/*` call, hence no `SESSION_LOCKED` and no `ESCROW_FAILED` in the error surface; user-facing copy must say "no share is sent to your server", never "your server is never contacted". `guard_self_held_kit_op` is the SEVENTH strict wallet allowlist and deliberately drops `guard_rekey_op`'s "current rotationKeys must be exactly 2" rule (which encodes the pre-inversion Custos `[device, PDS]` layout and would reject every claimed identity): device key pinned at `[0]`, the fresh recovery key inserted at `[1]`, the tail preserved verbatim, verificationMethods / services / alsoKnownAs byte-identical. `SelfHeldKitError` (NOT_DID_PLC, WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, HOST_OFFERS_ESCROW, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_SUBMISSION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, SHARE_NOT_STORED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/notifications.rs` — the device half of the end-to-end-encrypted notification relay (3 Tauri IPC commands): `register_for_notifications(did)` (`POST /v1/notifications/register` over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — device uuid, notification `did:key`, APNs token, and the app's own bundle id as the topic; re-pins on the same contact), `refresh_notification_sender_keys(did)` (`GET /v1/notifications/sender-keys`, the re-pin), and `get_notification_diagnostics()` (a no-network, no-identity read of what the device holds). **Device-global, not per-DID**: a push carries `{v, kid, enc, ct}` and nothing else — naming a DID would hand the relay and Apple the metadata the design exists to withhold — so the extension has no way to choose among per-identity keys, and there is one notification keypair and one `device_uuid` per install that every identity registers. **The pinned sender-key set is nonetheless per hosting server**, because `kid` is an autoincrement column on *one* instance and two instances will both publish a `kid` of 1 for unrelated keys; the extension tries every candidate under the incoming `kid` and HPKE Auth mode fails closed on a wrong one. A successful fetch **replaces that host's set wholesale** — that single choice is what implements add-new / retire / revoke: a revoked key vanishes from the device at its next contact, which is the entire short-compromise-window property. A 501 (host runs no relay) and a 503 (instance cannot read its own keys) both leave the stored set untouched: neither is a revocation, and clearing on a misconfigured deploy would strip every device that checked in during it. Two ordinary "no" answers are **outcomes, not errors** — `AWAITING_APNS_TOKEN` (simulator, denied permission, or the token simply not delivered yet) and `UNSUPPORTED` (a 501) — so onboarding has nothing to catch. A fourth command, `clear_notification_failures()`, and the `notification-failures` slot run the **other way**: the Notification Service Extension (`ios/NotificationService/`) appends to that slot and this module only reads it. iOS cannot let an extension suppress an alert push, so a payload that fails to verify still produces a banner — the honest "couldn't verify" notice, which on its own is a mystery. The breadcrumbs are what let Settings distinguish a key desync (open the app; it re-pins) from a relay sending junk (nothing at risk; consider another relay), which are the same banner and opposite responses. Read **fail-open** and with `reason` typed as a plain `String`: the extension is a separate bundle that versions independently, so an unrecognized reason must reach the screen generically rather than be dropped — the entry a stricter reader would discard is the one the user is asking about. `NotificationsError` (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, KEY_GENERATION_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/apns.rs` — **iOS-only** APNs device-token bridge. iOS delivers the token to two application-delegate methods and exposes it nowhere else, so this installs those methods on Tauri's live delegate class at startup (`objc2::ffi::class_addMethod` via `objc2-ui-kit`/`objc2-user-notifications`) and then asks for permission. **Add, never swizzle**: `class_addMethod` fails if the selector already exists, and that failure is the desired one — Tauri does not implement either method today, and silently displacing its implementation if it ever did would be far worse than declining and logging. The IMP is a bare C function pointer with no capture, so the callback reads the `AppHandle` from a `OnceLock` written during `setup` (the unit-of-global shape `IdentityStore` uses). On a **changed** token it re-registers every managed identity; an unchanged one (iOS re-delivers on every launch) does nothing, since a round trip per identity per launch would only rewrite rows that already say this. Every part with logic worth testing lives in `notifications.rs` — this file is compiled only by the `aarch64-apple-ios` cross-compile and exercised only on a device
- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)
- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (6 Tauri IPC commands): `get_identity_removal_route(did) -> RemovalRoute { requiresPassword, pdsUrl }` (which credential this identity's removal needs — `requiresPassword: false` when the host advertises `walletAccountDelete` and the wallet can sign the removal itself; resolved through the **same** `resolve_pds_url` the confirm step uses, so the screen and the request can never address different hosts; a host that could not be described reports `true`, since a field the user can ignore beats a missing one), `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `unlockIdentity` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password: Option<String>, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad credential mutates nothing — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`. `password: None` is an identity that has none: `build_delete_credential` then device-key-signs `crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope` — audience = the host's own `describeServer` DID, so a proof cannot be relayed to another server — and sends it as the body's off-lexicon `custos.proof`, gated on the host advertising `walletAccountDelete` (`PasswordRequired` otherwise, before anything is signed or sent). One `describeServer` answers both halves the proof needs — whether the host reads it, and the audience DID — so an unreachable host surfaces as the network failure it is rather than as a demand for a password the identity may not have. The server's refusal is deliberately identical for a bad password and a bad proof, so the wallet distinguishes them from what it *sent*: `InvalidToken` when a password went, `InvalidConfirmationCode` when a proof did — an identity with no password is never told to check one), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid (null when the removed DID has no tombstone leg — a did:web), wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalRoute` { requiresPassword, pdsUrl }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, INVALID_CONFIRMATION_CODE, PASSWORD_REQUIRED, PROOF_SIGNING_FAILED, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. Pure helpers: `guard_migration_op` (strict allowlist), `recommended_verification_methods`/`recommended_services` (RecommendedCredentials JSON → typed maps), `latest_op_state` (current state from newest non-nullified audit entry), `build_migration_diff`. Types: `SignedMigrationOp` { diff, signed_op }, `MigrationState` { did, dest_oauth_client, signed_op }, `MigrationInputs`; `MigrateError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_RECOMMENDED_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MIGRATION_NOT_READY). The destination-PDS OAuth login is NOT owned here — the migration orchestrator authenticates and populates `MigrationState.dest_oauth_client` before `build_migration_op_cmd` runs
- `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). Fine-grained per-step Tauri commands driving the source→dest transfer: `prepare_migration` (resolve dest describeServer + source; returns `PreparedMigration { handle, sourcePdsUrl }` for the source-auth screen), `authenticate_migration_source` (password `createSession` → full-session Bearer client, mirrors `claim::authenticate_source_pds`; per ADR-0021 a full session is required to mint the source's `createAccount` service-auth token — HTTPS + account-match guards + email-2FA, password used once and never stored), `create_destination_account` (reserveSigningKey → getServiceAuth → deactivated `createAccount` → Bearer session; tolerates `DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `transfer_repo` (getRepo → importRepo; on a source `getRepo` failure it falls back to the local iCloud repo mirror `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` when that mirror holds a CID/commit-valid snapshot for the DID, else surfaces the original source failure unchanged — the repo twin of the blob drain's mirror fallback), `transfer_blobs` (cursor-paginated `listMissingBlobs` drain), `transfer_preferences` (get→put), `verify_import` (`checkAccountStatus` completeness gate; returns `AccountStatus`), `arm_identity_leg` (populate `migrate::MigrationState.dest_oauth_client`, then run `migrate::build_migration_op_cmd`/`submit_migration_op_cmd`), `finalize_migration` (the safe cutover — **activate dest → durably persist the destination session → deactivate source → Finalized**; the source stays active until the durable credential is stored, so a crash or retry never strands the account credential-less). **Which credential gets persisted is capability-gated, not assumed**: `destination_credential` (pure, unit-tested) answers `Sovereign` or `Bearer` from the DID method plus the destination's advertised `sovereignSessions` (`pds_capabilities`, warm from `prepare_migration`'s describeServer). A host that **answered** and does not advertise it — the reference PDS, bsky.social, any spec-compliant PDS, or a Custos running with the capability off — takes the Bearer branch, since minting against a route it does not serve would fail *after* the identity op already landed. A did:web takes it unconditionally (no rotation keys to sign the proof). A host that could **not be asked** keeps the sovereign branch: `activateAccount` has already succeeded against it by then, so `reached: false` is a describeServer blink, not grounds to downgrade a Custos destination's credential. The same branch serves outbound migration and sovereign disaster recovery, which share this command. Pure cores split out for testability (`ensure_phase_did` gate, `create_destination_account_impl`, `drain_missing_blobs`, `transfer_repo_impl`, `transfer_preferences_impl`, `import_reconciles`, `activate_destination_account`/`deactivate_source_account` cutover halves, `destination_credential`, `ensure_sovereign_session_persisted` (idempotent skip when a persisted record's refresh token is still unexpired, else `sovereign_session::sovereign_login_impl` → persist), `ensure_bearer_session_persisted` (the same idempotent skip, then sub/aud-validate and persist the pair `createAccount` already issued into the same `{did}:oauth-tokens` record — from that write on `session_provider` restores and refreshes it identically, and re-unlock rides `password_unlock`'s password `createSession` route), and the `*_core` mutex-parameterized command cores; `finalize_migration_core` takes an injected `ensure_session` step so its activate → session → deactivate ordering is unit-testable without a Keychain or live PDS, and `finalize_migration_impl` sits above it holding the whole snapshot → capability probe → branch → cutover path, so everything the Tauri command does bar unwrapping `State` is drivable against mock servers — which is what proves the non-Custos cutover never calls `/v1/sessions/sovereign`). `MigrationError` (MIGRATION_NOT_READY, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED, ACCOUNT_CREATION_FAILED, DESTINATION_CONFLICT, REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED, BLOB_TRANSFER_FAILED, PREFERENCES_TRANSFER_FAILED, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE, ACTIVATION_FAILED, SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED, SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED, DEACTIVATION_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR — SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED and SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED are the retryable cutover-mint failures that leave the source active, aborting before deactivation). Migration state is in-memory only (`AppState.orchestration_state`); an app kill restarts from `prepare_migration`, but the destination session it persists (via `identity_store` `{did}:oauth-tokens`) survives — a restarted wallet reconstructs the destination client from that record (`sovereign_session::stored_bearer_client`), not from `OutboundMigrationState`. The orchestrator never POSTs plc.directory — the single PLC write is `migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`
- `src/disaster_recovery.rs` — Sovereign disaster recovery (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Rebuild from backup" on the identity screen): rebuild the account on a new (or the same) PDS from the iCloud backups when the source PDS is gone or uncooperative, the ATProto "adversarial migration" pattern automated by the wallet's custody of `rotationKeys[0]`. `prepare_disaster_recovery(did, dest_pds_url, handle_override?)` (resolve the destination `describeServer` DID + current PLC state from plc.directory alone — the dead source is never contacted; `handle_override` is the fallback for a handle whose domain the dead PDS served; opens a `recovery: true` orchestration session), `enroll_recovery_signing_key(did)` (PLC op #1: generate — or reuse across retries — a self-controlled P-256 `atproto` signing key, persist its scalar to the per-DID `recovery-signing-key` Keychain slot with read-back verify BEFORE any network call, then build + device-key-sign + submit the enroll op directly to plc.directory; reconciles to success if a prior attempt already landed; biometric-gated in the frontend), `await_recovery_key_visibility(did)` (one audit-log poll: is the enrolled key the DID's `atproto` method yet? advances the phase gate when it is — `createAccount` cannot run before op #1 propagates), `create_recovery_destination_account(did, email, invite_code?)` (re-verify visibility, mint the service-auth JWT **offline** with the self-controlled key — `iss` = account DID, `aud` = destination server DID, `lxm` = `com.atproto.server.createAccount`, 1h expiry, via `crypto::mint_service_auth_jwt` — and run the shared migration `createAccount` core; the destination verifies the JWT against plc.directory, so this works against any PDS), and `recovery_transfer_repo(app, did)` (importRepo from the validated iCloud CAR via `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car`; `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` when no valid snapshot exists). The transfer tail reuses the orchestrator's shared commands against the same session: `transfer_blobs` (mirror-primary — the drain reads `mirror_fallback_blob` directly, no doomed source fetches), `transfer_preferences` (honest no-op skip: no preferences backup exists), `verify_import`, `arm_identity_leg` + the `migrate.rs` identity leg (PLC op #2: adopt the destination's recommended keys + `services` repoint, wallet device key still at `rotationKeys[0]`), and `finalize_migration` (activate the destination; no source to deactivate). The strict pre-sign guard `guard_recovery_enroll_op` is the FIFTH wallet allowlist and the narrowest: ONLY the `atproto` verification method may change, to exactly the freshly generated key (fresh = not a rotation key, not an existing method) — rotationKeys must be byte-identical with the device key at `[0]` (the anti-lockout rule from the adversarial-migration write-up), alsoKnownAs and services preserved (the `atproto_pds` repoint belongs to op #2). The created account stays deactivated until the final activation, so an abort at any earlier step leaves nothing half-live; a stolen device key attempting this is caught by `plc_monitor` + the 72-hour recovery window. `DisasterRecoveryError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, KEY_NOT_ENROLLED, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, RECOVERY_NOT_READY, NETWORK_ERROR) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields; the orchestration-half commands return `MigrationError` (whose `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` variant is recovery-specific)
- `src/endpoint_repair.rs` — sovereign "repair hosting endpoint" flow for a wallet-custodied did:plc (1 Tauri IPC command, `repair_hosting_endpoint(did, new_endpoint)`): when the hosting server changes hostname underneath the account, the DID document's `atproto_pds` endpoint points at a dead host and every client misroutes — and a passwordless account can only mint the session the server-signed `signPlcOperation` path needs against that same dead host. So the wallet device-key-signs the repoint itself and submits DIRECTLY to plc.directory; the only network dependencies are plc.directory and the NEW endpoint, never the old one. The new endpoint is normalized to a bare https origin (`normalize_endpoint`) and probed via the public `com.atproto.sync.getRepoStatus` to prove it actually hosts this DID before anything signs (`DESTINATION_NOT_HOSTING` otherwise). `guard_endpoint_repair` is the SIXTH strict wallet allowlist and the narrowest service mutation: ONLY the `atproto_pds` endpoint string may change — rotationKeys, verificationMethods, alsoKnownAs, every other service, and even the `atproto_pds` service type must be byte-identical, and a no-op endpoint must reconcile (an already-correct document returns success with `opCid: null`) rather than sign. `EndpointRepairError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, INVALID_ENDPOINT, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, DESTINATION_NOT_HOSTING, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields; the frontend gates `repairHostingEndpoint` behind `authenticateBiometric()`, and the `EndpointRepairScreen` is reached from AdvancedToolsScreen's "Repair hosting endpoint" row, behind the vestibule (root-key did:plc only)
- `src/handle_change.rs` — sovereign "change handle" flow for a wallet-custodied did:plc. Two Tauri commands: `get_identity_handle_domains(did)` (discovers the DID's HOSTING PDS via `discover_pds`, returns its `describeServer.availableUserDomains` — distinct from the create flow's `get_available_user_domains`, which targets only the configured Custos) and `change_handle_cmd(did, handle)` — the full passwordless flow: resolve a full-access session (`session_provider::SessionProvider::full_access_client`), call `com.atproto.identity.updateHandle` on the hosting PDS (PDS arbitrates served-domain allocation / uniqueness / reserved names), then build + **device-key-sign** the `alsoKnownAs` PLC op via `crypto::build_did_plc_rotation_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and refresh the cached PLC log + DID doc. Ordering is `updateHandle` FIRST, PLC op SECOND (a failure between self-heals on retry: `build_handle_op` re-reads the audit log each attempt, and an op that already landed makes the desired `alsoKnownAs` current → reconciles to success without a re-POST). The strict pre-sign guard `guard_handle_change` is the THIRD wallet allowlist — the mirror image of `migrate::guard_migration_op`: **alsoKnownAs MAY change; rotationKeys, verificationMethods, and services must NOT** (+ device key must be in the current rotationKeys, else `WalletNotAuthorized`). Pure helpers: `guard_handle_change`, `latest_full_state` (full current state incl. VMs + services maps), `compute_new_also_known_as` (new `at://{handle}` primary, prior `at://` handles dropped, non-handle aliases preserved), `classify_update_handle_error`. `HandleChangeError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, SESSION_LOCKED{reason}, RATE_LIMITED, HANDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE, INVALID_HANDLE, UPDATE_HANDLE_FAILED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) — `SESSION_LOCKED` carries the `session_provider::UnlockReason` and is the cue for the frontend to run `unlockIdentity(did)` and retry. A directory read (`fetch_audit_log`/`fetch_plc_data_document`/`discover_pds`) is classified via `map_plc_fetch_error` (throttle → RATE_LIMITED, HTTP verdict → PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, transport → NETWORK_ERROR) and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (a server verdict/unsupported-host/keychain/malformed-response failure → SERVER_ERROR, never NETWORK_ERROR). The biometric gate is in the frontend (`$lib/ipc/handle-change.ts`'s `changeHandle`), in front of the Secure-Enclave signing
- `src/rotate_repo_key.rs` — sovereign repo signing-key rotation for a wallet-custodied did:plc (ADR-0025): replace the PDS-held commit-signing key (`verificationMethods.atproto` / the PDS `rotationKeys` slot) with a freshly generated one — the recovery move when the PDS key's at-rest encryption is compromised or its master key is lost. Two Tauri commands: `build_repo_key_rotation_cmd(did) -> SignedRotationOp` (resolve a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`, `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation` on the hosting PDS to stage a fresh key, fetch the audit log via `handle_change::latest_full_state`, compose the op — device key stays `rotationKeys[0]`, staged key takes the PDS slot + the `atproto` method, services/alsoKnownAs preserved — run the strict guard, device-key-sign via `crypto::build_did_plc_rotation_op`, park in `AppState.rotation_state`) and `submit_repo_key_rotation_cmd(did) -> ClaimResult` (`POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation/complete` with the parked op — **the wallet never POSTs this op to plc.directory itself**: the PDS submits it and cuts its commit signer over atomically under the account's repo write lock, so no commit is ever signed by a key absent from the DID doc — then refresh the cached PLC log + DID doc; the PDS side is retry-safe, so the op stays parked until success). `guard_rotation_op` is the FOURTH strict wallet allowlist: **the atproto verification method and the PDS rotationKeys slot move to exactly the PDS-staged key; rotationKeys must be exactly `[device, staged]`, other verificationMethods entries, services, and alsoKnownAs must NOT change** (+ device key must be in the current rotationKeys, else `WalletNotAuthorized`; a staged key already present in the doc is rejected as non-fresh). Pure helpers: `guard_rotation_op`, `build_rotation_diff`. `RotationError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, SESSION_LOCKED{reason}, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, ROTATION_FAILED{status}, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, NO_PENDING_ROTATION) — directory reads classify via `map_plc_fetch_error` and session-lifecycle failures via `map_session_error`, the same split as `HandleChangeError`. The biometric gate is in the frontend (`$lib/ipc/rotation.ts`'s `submitRepoKeyRotation`), in front of the irreversible submission
- `src/lib.rs::check_identity_status() -> Result<Vec<IdentityStatus>, MonitorError>` — Tauri IPC command (delegates to `PlcMonitor::check_all`)
- `src/lib.rs::list_identities() -> Result<Vec<String>, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: returns managed DIDs from Keychain via `IdentityStore::list_identities()`; returns empty list if no identities claimed
- `src/lib.rs::get_stored_did_doc(did: String) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: retrieves stored DID document as parsed JSON for a claimed identity; returns None if not stored
- `src/lib.rs::get_device_key_id(did: String) -> Result<String, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: returns the device key's did:key URI for a claimed identity via `IdentityStore::get_or_create_device_key()`
- `src/sovereign_session.rs::sovereign_login(did: String) -> Result<SovereignLoginResult, SovereignLoginError>` — Tauri IPC command: mints and persists a full-access Bearer session with the selected DID's current rotation key; frontend callers use `sovereignLogin(did)`, which gates the IPC call behind `authenticateBiometric()` so cancellation signs and sends nothing
- `src/session_provider.rs::ensure_identity_session(did: String) -> Result<SessionReady, SessionError>` — Tauri IPC command: the frontend pre-flight. Restores or rotates the DID's session and reports status (dropping the in-Rust client); a `NEEDS_UNLOCK` error is the cue for the UI to run `unlockIdentity(did)` — the passwordless `sovereignLogin(did)` where the host advertises `sovereignSessions`, the `password_unlock` prompt where it does not. Performs **no** biometric prompt — a live token must never demand one. Frontend wrapper: `ensureIdentitySession(did)`.
- `src/lib.rs::register_created_identity(did: String, handle: String) -> Result<(), RegisterIdentityError>` — Tauri IPC command: registers a just-created identity in `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` (the create flow otherwise writes only the OAuth session + legacy `"did"` Keychain item, which the home screen does not read). Calls `add_identity` (tolerating `IdentityAlreadyExists`), `adopt_global_device_key` (so the per-DID key matches the genesis rotation key), and stores a locally-built PLC-format DID document (handle + PDS + rotationKeys). Mirrors `claim::submit_claim`'s persistence step. `RegisterIdentityError` { KEYCHAIN_ERROR } serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`
- `src/lib.rs::get_pds_url() -> Option<String>` — Tauri IPC command: loads PDS base URL from Keychain, returns Some(url) if configured or None for first-launch
- `src/lib.rs::save_pds_url(url: String) -> Result<(), PdsConfigError>` — Tauri IPC command: validates URL format, pings `/xrpc/_health` on the PDS, saves to Keychain, initializes `AppState.custos_client` (runtime configuration), then re-probes the host's advertised capabilities into `pds_capabilities`'s per-host cache (best-effort — the user has just deliberately re-pointed the wallet, which is exactly when a stale verdict would be wrong)
- `src/lib.rs::get_pds_capabilities(pds_url: Option<String>) -> Result<ServerCapabilities, PdsConfigError>` — Tauri IPC command: what the configured PDS (or a named one) advertises, so a screen offers only host-supported features. Cached per host; **an absent `custos` extension and an unreachable host both report an empty list** rather than erroring, so a gate degrades to standard-lexicon behavior instead of failing. Rejects only for a malformed URL
- `src/lib.rs::get_appearance_preference() -> Option<String>` — Tauri IPC command: returns the saved appearance preference (`"system"` | `"light"` | `"dark"`) from the Keychain, or None if never set; a corrupt/unrecognized stored value reads as None (follow the system), never an error
- `src/lib.rs::set_appearance_preference(preference: String) -> Result<(), AppearanceError>` — Tauri IPC command: validates the value against the three-value allowlist and persists it to the Keychain. `AppearanceError` { INVALID_PREFERENCE, KEYCHAIN_ERROR } serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`

**Guarantees:**
- `crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` supports iOS (staticlib), Android (cdylib), and normal cargo builds (rlib)
- `src/main.rs` is the desktop entry point; `src/lib.rs::run()` is the iOS/Android entry point (via `#[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]`)
- `tauri.conf.json` configures the bundle identifier, dev URL (`http://localhost:5173`), and frontend dist path (`../dist`)
- `create_account` maps PDS HTTP error codes to typed `CreateAccountError` variants (EXPIRED_CODE, REDEEMED_CODE, EMAIL_TAKEN, HANDLE_TAKEN, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE" }` for the frontend
- `perform_did_ceremony` maps failures to typed `DIDCeremonyError` variants (KEY_NOT_FOUND, PDS_KEY_FETCH_FAILED, NO_PDS_SIGNING_KEY, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_CREATION_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` for the frontend; `confirm_share_backup` maps to `ShareBackupError` (SHARE_NOT_STORED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `prepare_oauth_flow` / `complete_oauth_flow` map failures to typed `OAuthError` variants (DPOP_KEY_GEN_FAILED, DPOP_KEY_INVALID, DPOP_PROOF_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, STATE_MISMATCH, CALLBACK_ABANDONED, PAR_FAILED, TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FAILED, TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED, INVALID_GRANT, NOT_AUTHENTICATED) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` for the frontend
- The OAuth callback is delivered by **`ASWebAuthenticationSession`** (via the vendored `tauri-plugin-auth-session`), **not** a deep link. The frontend calls `prepare_*` (Rust) for the authorize URL, then `plugin:auth-session|start` (which opens the in-app auth sheet and returns the `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback?code=...&state=...` URL), then `complete_*` (Rust) to finish. The custom scheme `org.obsign.identitywallet` is registered in `src-tauri/Info.ios.plist` (`CFBundleURLTypes`, alongside the legacy `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` transition entry) because it is the session's `callbackURLScheme`. **Why not deep links:** iOS Safari will not auto-launch the app from a server-side redirect to a custom scheme, so the old `tauri-plugin-deep-link` + `on_open_url` + `handle_deep_link` flow silently failed; ASWebAuthenticationSession captures the callback itself
- On app startup, if OAuth tokens exist in Keychain, the session is restored into `AppState.oauth_session` and an `auth_ready` Tauri event is emitted after a 300ms delay (allows SvelteKit to boot and register its listener)
- `OAuthClient` transparently refreshes access tokens with <60s remaining before each request; retries once on `use_dpop_nonce` 400 responses from the server. A 400 that is NOT a `use_dpop_nonce` challenge (a genuine `InvalidRequest`/`InsufficientScope`/etc.) is buffered and handed back to the caller as an intact `reqwest::Response` (rebuilt via `http::Response` → `reqwest::Response::from`), NOT flattened into `NotAuthenticated` — so the caller's classifier (`pds_client::classify_xrpc_response`) can surface the server's real status + body on the DPoP migration-source path. Non-400 statuses were already passed through untouched
- `DPoPKeypair` is idempotent: `get_or_create()` generates and persists to Keychain on first call, loads from Keychain on subsequent calls; the same key is used across all DPoP proofs and app sessions
- `device_key::get_or_create()` is idempotent -- returns the same key on every call for a given device
- `device_key::sign()` returns raw 64-byte r||s ECDSA signatures; low-S normalized on both paths (ATProto/PLC directory requires low-S); deterministic (RFC 6979) on simulator
- `DeviceKeyError` variants serialize as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` matching the `CreateAccountError` pattern
